body.statement: The certificate criterion is necessary and sufficient: \(\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\). On the affirmative side, \(\mathsf A\) returns \(\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}\); on the negative side, it returns \(\mathsf{Wit}_{T,S,B}\). This equivalence holds simultaneously for every endpoint coordinate \(Q_a(x)\) and every positive law, including null allowed-arrow effects and deficient observable-kernel ranks.
body.justification: An iff theorem distinguishes a design rule from another sufficient recovery recipe and makes failure operational through a legal countermodel.
body.gap: Theorems 1--6 of Tikka and Karvanen neither use partial audit margins nor characterize intervention-target identification; Levis et al. require full phase-two recovery.
body.consumer: The theorem decides whether a planned partial recontact protocol supports the five-year treatment-specific weight distribution in an EHR cohort under the declared local dropout graph.

obligation.what_is_open: The theorem awaits the exhaustive recovery-or-witness alternative posed by the open-ended question.
obligation.obstruction: Neither \(\mathsf A\) nor its branch invariant has been defined, so recovery soundness and obstruction completeness cannot be used as proved premises. Treating the certificate handle itself as that theorem would assume the crux.
obligation.attempted: I reduced both directions of the claimed equivalence to the two outputs required from the missing alternative and checked that audit-table equivalence supplies the necessary passage from observed laws to pattern tables.
obligation.partial_result:
If the requested exhaustive alternative were proved for a specified
procedure \(\mathsf A\), the equivalence theorem would follow immediately
and without an additional regularity premise.  Indeed, on a recovery
branch, equality of the laws of \(O\) implies equality of every \(M_d\) by
the audit-table proposition, and hence
\[
Q(P)=\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}((M_d(P))_{d=0}^T)
    =\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}((M_d(P'))_{d=0}^T)=Q(P').
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\).  On an obstruction branch, the
returned pair satisfies equal observed laws and unequal target vectors,
which is exactly a counterexample to graphwise identification.  This
argument also shows that vector identification, null allowed-arrow
effects, and deficient ranks require no separate logical step once the
alternative itself is available.  What is missing is the premise of this
reduction: the exhaustive alternative has not been constructed or proved.
